scenarios.title: Join two LAN segments with a Linux bridge
scenarios.summary: Connect two untagged LAN segments with a Linux bridge, keep the host address on the bridge, and explain which paths remain when one port is unavailable.
scenarios.objective: Prepare the four saved virtual profiles for the next simulated startup: put a usable address with the supplied LAN prefix on br0, distinct from the two workstations, and attach both intended physical NICs as bridge ports. With both ports available, br0 must reach both workstations and the workstations must have a two-way untagged path through the bridge. When a physical port is unavailable, retain the reachable segment and keep the two segments isolated; do not invent bond-style failover. Keep the current bridge IP settings, controller configuration and attached membership unchanged while re-reading saved files. Keep audit.nmconnection unchanged, keep Audit reachable on mgmt0 and add no default route there. Retain all four supplied filenames and UUIDs. Choose Test startup profiles and inspect all three physical cases.

steps: Inspect the four saved profiles, repair the controller and missing port, then test all three cases while preserving the supplied current bridge and Audit.
scenarios.explanation: br0 is a software bridge joining two untagged segments. Its manual host address belongs to the common supplied LAN; a different usable address can work if it does not duplicate either workstation. The controller starts matching bound ports when autoconnect-ports=1, even with port autoconnect=false. Both ports forward in the supplied settled tree. A missing binding or down port isolates that segment rather than choosing a backup NIC as a bond would. Current parsed IP/control/membership snapshots remain separate from edited future files. Passing all three cases means matching the expected available and blocked paths, not making a disconnected cable work.
hints: Compare the saved br0 address and prefix with the supplied LAN. Put host addressing on the bridge controller; the physical ports have no separate host address in this task.
Inspect autoconnect-ports in bridge.nmconnection and the two binding keys in port-enp2s0.nmconnection. An unbound Ethernet candidate is not a bridge port.
After testing, select each physical case. The unavailable segment should remain isolated while the other segment and Audit stay usable. Read current and next-startup settings separately.
scenarios.simplifications: One source-bound bridge and two physical ports in a supplied acyclic untagged tree; manual IPv4 on the controller, separate Audit interface, explicit current/future snapshots and three fixed physical cases. Both-direction broadcast delivery is a bounded Layer2 proof, not real ping, IP forwarding, MAC learning or a packet capture. No tagged traffic, VLAN filtering, STP election/convergence/timers, hairpin/multicast options, independent port-driven startup/discovery, general nmcli/ip, DHCP/IPv6 bridge, nested controllers, host files/services/devices, daemon/kernel/boot or network operations. NM STP defaults enabled; accepting disabled STP in this supplied tree is not evidence of general loop safety. Each down-port case has explicit expected isolated paths.
